analysis.verdict: Ibnsina Pharma is a growing, market-leading business whose share price is in a confirmed downtrend. The stock has lost 39% from its August peak and trades below both its 50-day and 200-day averages. Earnings are still rising, the shares look cheap against analyst targets near EGP 16.5, and the company is buying back stock. Against that, the October rate hike lands directly on its interest bill. This is a stock to watch for a turn, and the tracker is built to flag that turn when it shows up in the price.

p: Ibnsina Pharma is Egypt's largest pharmaceutical distributor. It buys medicines from manufacturers and delivers them to pharmacies, hospitals and wholesalers across the country. It reported a 29.1% share of the market for the first half of 2026 (IQVIA data, adjusted for the reclassification of Ezaby as a distributor), after 30.8% in 2024 and 24.2% in 2023.

Distribution is a high-volume, thin-margin trade. Gross margin is about 8% and EBITDA margin about 4-5%. Because drug prices in Egypt are set by the regulator, the company cannot simply raise prices. Profit depends on volume growth, the discount it earns from manufacturers, cost control, and above all the cost of the bank borrowing that funds its inventory and receivables.

Growth is strong. Full-year 2025 net profit was EGP 951.8m, up 54.9%. First-half 2026 net sales reached EGP 41.5bn (up about 18%) and net profit EGP 511.3m (up 31.5%), helped by lower borrowing costs during the easing cycle that ran until this autumn.

Two things have weakened. Gross margin fell from 8.7% to 8.0% in the first half as sales shifted toward hospitals and non-pharma lines (management guides to 8.2% for the year), and first-quarter EBITDA margin dropped to 3.8% from 5.1%. Leverage also rose: net debt went from 1.4x EBITDA in March to 2.15x in June.

On my estimate of roughly 1.04bn shares after last year's treasury-share cancellation, the stock trades near 10 times trailing earnings. Treat that as approximate and check the share count before relying on it. Dividends over the past year total EGP 0.26 a share, a yield of about 2.5%. The three analysts covering the stock have a consensus target of about EGP 16.5.

The shares rose from about EGP 2.3 in November 2023 to an intraday high of EGP 16.93 on 4 August 2026, a day that closed far lower at 13.37 on record volume of 46.7m shares. That reversal marked the top. The price then slid to 11.5 by late September, broke down on 25 October with an 8.4% one-day fall, and bottomed at 9.02 on 3 November.

Since then it has bounced to 10.33 (close of 12 November), 14.5% above the low and 39% below the high. Annualised volatility is about 40%, so swings of 2-3% a day are normal for this stock. Average turnover is about 5.5m shares or EGP 63m a day, which is liquid enough for retail-sized orders.
The primary trend is down: price (10.33) is below the 50-day average (11.29), which is below the 200-day (11.57). That crossover happened in recent weeks and usually takes time to repair.

Short-term momentum has turned up. MACD crossed above its signal line during the bounce and RSI has recovered from oversold to a neutral 47. This is what a relief rally inside a downtrend looks like. It becomes something more only if price reclaims the 50-day and 200-day averages.
bullets: Support: 9.02 (the 3 November low). A close below it reopens the decline.
First resistance: 11.26 to 11.29 (the 20-day high and the 50-day average).
Trend resistance: 11.57 (the 200-day average). A close above it is the first real sign the downtrend is over.

p: The EGX30 fell to about 48,400 in early November and has recovered to 52,023. On 29 October the Central Bank of Egypt surprised the market with a 100 bps rate increase, its first since March 2024, taking the deposit rate to 20% and the lending rate to 21%. Inflation is running near 13% against a 7% target, and the bank projects it higher in fiscal 2026/27.

High rates hurt this stock twice. They raise Ibnsina's own interest expense, and 20%+ yields on treasury bills pull local money out of equities. The pound has steadied near EGP 53.4 to the dollar on foreign demand for debt, which removes one source of pressure for now.

sections.h: What would make it a buy
bullets: Price closes back above the 200-day average (about 11.57) with the 50-day turning up.
Third-quarter results show margins holding near 8.2% and interest costs under control.
The central bank signals that the October hike was a one-off.
The buyback is executed in size, or analysts hold their targets after the results.

sections.h: What would make it a sell
bullets: A close below 9.02 on heavy volume.
Third-quarter results showing a further margin squeeze or a jump in finance costs.
Another rate hike or a renewed slide in the pound.
A regulatory change to distributor margins or drug pricing.
Third-quarter 2026 results. Sources give dates between mid-November and 2 December.
The central bank's December rate meeting.
Execution of the 1% treasury share buyback approved in late October.
Monthly inflation prints and moves in the pound.
